title: A Roman Street Watched Audrey Hepburn for Four Months. All Fourteen of Them Were Wrong.
title_alternatives: A Roman Street Watched Audrey Hepburn for Four Months. All Fourteen of Them Were Wrong.
Every Thursday She Walked the Last Three Streets on Foot. The Neighbours Thought They Knew Why.
Fourteen People Saw Her. Not One of Them Guessed She Was Reading a Newspaper Out Loud.
The Old Woman Never Knew Who Her Thursday Visitor Was. Audrey Hepburn Never Told Her.
A Shoemaker Kept Her Secret for 35 Years. He Told It Six Weeks Before He Died.
description:
Between September 1960 and January 1961, a woman came to a poor street on the eastern side of Rome roughly once a week, always after dark, always alone, and always on foot for the last three hundred metres.

Fourteen people saw her. Not one of them saw more than about ninety seconds of any visit. This story is made out of those fourteen fragments — and every single one of them was wrong.

Not slightly wrong, in the way witnesses usually are, about the colour of a coat or the hour. Wrong about the entire nature of what they were looking at, all fourteen, for four months.

The street built three theories: a married man, a debt, an illness. What none of them could explain was the walking. She could have been driven to the door. She never was.

The boy on the second floor saw the most and understood the least, which is usually how it goes. He remembered the parcel that went up and never came down, the stop on the third landing every time, and a piano playing the same four bars over and over. He assumed for thirty-eight years that it was somebody learning. It was the exact opposite of that.

What was actually happening in that room can be told in four sentences, and there is no scandal in it anywhere — which is exactly why a street looking for one could not see it.

The reason she never explained is the whole story, and it has nothing to do with shame.

This story is a work of fiction. Elsa, Nardo, Tonino, the street and every detail in it are invented, created for storytelling and not drawn from any record.
